title: EU Policy and Outreach Partnerships (POP) and Cultural Relations Platform Overview
executive_summary: The EU Policy and Outreach Partnerships (POP), established under the EU Foreign Policy Instrument, aim to enhance the EU’s engagement with partner countries through public diplomacy, focusing on improving understanding of the European project and deepening connections with future leaders in key policy areas, including culture. As of 2020, ten POP and related support programmes are active across regions such as the USA, Canada, Mexico and Central America, South America, Russia, China, Indonesia, India, South Korea, and Japan. Activities include support and cooperation in cultural and creative sectors, facilitation of cultural exchanges, promotion of EU cultural initiatives, and capacity-building. These efforts are designed to foster cultural relations, diplomacy, and cooperation, particularly in fragile contexts, thereby strengthening the EU’s global presence and influence.
characteristics: The EU Policy and Outreach Partnerships (POP) are initiatives under the EU Foreign Policy Instrument (FPI) aimed at engaging partner country audiences through public diplomacy, activities, tools, and training.

POP’s objectives include improving understanding of the European project among partner country citizens and deepening EU engagement with future leaders and influencers, especially in key policy areas like culture.
Ten POP programmes are implemented globally, including in the USA, Canada, Mexico and Central America, South America, Russia, China, Indonesia, India, Republic of Korea, and Japan.

Activities include support and cooperation in cultural and creative sectors, facilitation of cultural exchanges and matchmaking, cultural cooperation in fragile contexts, promotion of EU prizes and outreach, cultural relations and diplomacy strategies, and capacity-building.
practical_applications: Implementation of the EU Policy and Outreach Partnerships (POP) programmes in multiple regions, including South America (Argentina, Brazil, Chile, Colombia, Peru, Uruguay), USA, Canada, Mexico and Central America, Russia, China, Indonesia, India, Republic of Korea, and Japan, supporting public diplomacy activities, tools, and training to engage with partner country audiences.

Active support and cooperation initiatives in the cultural and creative sectors through POP, including facilitation of cultural exchanges and matchmaking, cultural cooperation in fragile contexts, promotion of EU prizes and European Capitals of Culture (ECOC), and outreach activities.
Ongoing capacity-building activities and the development of cultural relations and diplomacy strategies as part of the POP framework.

Operation of specific support facilities such as the Policy Dialogue Support Facility in India and the Republic of Korea, and the Support Facility for the implementation of the EU-Japan Strategic Partnership Agreement.

top_actors.name: European Union
top_actors.justification: The European Union is the central actor in the document, as the POP initiatives are designed, funded, and implemented under its auspices. The text repeatedly references the EU as the main driver of policy, outreach, and cultural diplomacy activities, and all listed programmes are EU-led.

top_actors.name: European Commission
top_actors.justification: The European Commission, specifically through the Foreign Policy Instrument (FPI), is responsible for building and managing the POP. Its role is crucial in operationalizing the EU's external cultural relations and public diplomacy, making it highly influential in the context.

top_actors.name: EU Delegations
top_actors.justification: EU Delegations are implied as key implementers of the POP activities in partner countries. While not as prominently mentioned as the EU or the Commission, their role in engaging with local audiences and executing the initiatives on the ground is significant.

top_themes.name: Bi-regional Cooperation
top_themes.justification: The document's main focus is on the EU Policy and Outreach Partnerships (POP), which are designed to foster cooperation and engagement between the EU and partner countries across multiple regions. The text details the implementation of POP programmes in various regions (e.g., USA, Canada, South America, etc.), highlighting bi-regional cooperation as the central theme. This is directly tied to the EU's strategic objective of strengthening international relations and public diplomacy.

top_themes.name: Support & Cooperation in Cultural and Creative Sectors
top_themes.justification: A significant portion of the document is dedicated to describing activities such as support and cooperation in cultural and creative sectors, facilitation of cultural exchanges, and cultural diplomacy strategies. These activities are core to the POP's mission and are explicitly listed as key actions, underlining their strategic importance in achieving the EU's outreach and engagement goals.

top_themes.name: Digital & Technological Partnerships
top_themes.justification: While not explicitly detailed in the text, digital and technological partnerships are implied through the mention of public diplomacy tools, training, and capacity-building. These elements are important for modern international cooperation and outreach, but the document devotes less explicit content to this theme compared to bi-regional cooperation and cultural sector support.
